title: tracker.json
description: The tracker backend choice and its paths, in .human-in-the-lead/tracker.json (design parts 3.4 and 16.6). Every setting has a default, so a project that keeps the reference layout needs only schema_version. A project with an existing tracker in another place maps onto the layout here by configuration, not migration (design part 16.7). The ID key is policy.json's project.key.

backend.description: Which backend holds the tracker. Only the files backend exists in One signal end to end.

work_dir.description: The directory that holds the item folders and the generated views, relative to the repository root. Never absolute, never with a ".." segment.

folders.description: The folder name under work_dir for each group of files. Initiatives, projects and milestones have their own; work, decision and external items share one, so an item that changes kind does not move. Release records, one per release named by its tag, have their own folder too (design part 3.2, Milestones and releases).

views_dir.description: Where generated views are written, relative to work_dir. Only the merge queue regenerates and commits them, on the main branch.

lists_readme.description: A file under work_dir that holds the generated item lists between the markers <!-- work:lists:begin ... --> and <!-- work:lists:end -->. When set, `hitld work views` rewrites the text between them. Unset by default: the lists are written as a view file only. A relative path of plain segments, like work_dir.

main_branch.description: The branch the orchestrator creates items on and where claims are released. Claims are read from every other branch.

bundle_refs.description: Ref prefixes where bundles from another machine are fetched. Claim branches under them count as claims, so a second machine's claims show once its bundle is fetched (design part 3.2, Lifecycle).

optional_keys.description: Front-matter keys beyond the reference format that this project's items may carry. Empty by default: the reference format's check rejects every other key. Turning one on lets the check accept it and the tracker read and write it, typed as the item schema types it.

fields.description: Project-specific fields beyond the reference format and optional_keys. Each is declared with a name, a type, whether it holds a list, and a description. A declared field is validated against its type, kept when the tool rewrites a file, returned by the read API (hitld work show and query with --json) and usable in queries (--field). Names that the format already uses, and keys that tools run as code, are refused. Declared fields are strings in the file and typed on read.

default_classification.description: The classification of an item whose file does not say (the reference format has no such key). The check refuses an item above the repository's classification ceiling, so the default must not exceed it.

name.description: The front-matter key: lower case, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Unique among declared fields, and not a key the format uses.

type.description: string, integer (whole numbers), number or boolean (true or false). In a list, each member has this type.

list.description: True when the field holds a list of values of its type.

values.description: For a string field: the values it may take. Omitted means any text.

description.description: What the field is for, in one sentence.

path.description: A relative path of plain segments: no leading slash, no "..", no backslash.
